LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WanderingSwordsman_Text: A wandering swordsman stops at the edge of your land, tired and sword-sheathed. He says he has crossed three fragments of Jiuxiao and has not lost a duel since the Convergence, and he would like to leave something to someone worthy before his luck runs out.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WanderingSwordsman_Res_spar: Your best fighter learns more in an afternoon than in a month.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WanderingSwordsman_Opt_feed: Feed him and let him go
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WanderingSwordsman_Res_feed: He leaves a pouch of herbs and a story behind.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HermitTeaches_Text: An old hermit with a face like a dried plum walks into the colony as if he lived there. He does not say his name. He watches your cultivators breathe, clicks his tongue, and offers to correct them for the price of a bowl of rice.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HermitTeaches_Res_accept: The hermit rearranges a hand here, a breath there. By evening your cultivator's qi runs smoother.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HermitTeaches_Res_decline: He shrugs and walks into the dusk, whistling.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_LostDiscipleChild_Text: A boy in a robe too big for him sits at the roadside, holding a sword he cannot lift. His sect fell in the Calamity and he has been walking for weeks. He does not ask for anything: he only asks which direction is the east.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_LostDiscipleChild_Res_keep: He bows to every member of the colony, in turn, and will not be dissuaded.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_LostDiscipleChild_Res_direct: He thanks you and sets off, a very small figure on a very large road.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayDisciple_Text: A young disciple of the Formless Sword arrives wounded and begs for shelter. He says he saw something in the Sword Mound that the elders do not want known, and that the sect's enforcers are two days behind him. His story has a hole in it, but his wounds do not.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayDisciple_Res_hide: The disciple collapses in relief. Two days is not much time.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayDisciple_Res_hand: The enforcers thank you coldly and take him. Nobody in the colony meets his eyes.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayEnforcers_Label: The enforcers of the Sword Mound
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayEnforcers_Text: The enforcers of the Formless Sword have arrived, sword-hands resting on their hilts. They do not threaten: they only ask, politely, where the disciple is. They have the patience of people who know that the answer always comes.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayEnforcers_Res_protect: Swords come out. The disciple, from a loft, finally understands that he has chosen his side.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayEnforcers_Res_give: The enforcers lead him away. He does not resist, which is worse.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RunawayThanks_Text: When the dust settles the disciple tells his story to the end. In the Sword Mound, one of the swords had begun to whisper in the voice of the Iron Calamity. He has the proof wrapped in a cloth: a splinter of black metal that hums, and that he cannot bring himself to touch.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CursedBlade_Text: Your people find a long sword lying in a stream, perfect, unrusted, humming faintly. The old tales warn against any weapon that no one remembers losing. The old tales also say that the best swords were found, not made.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CursedBlade_Res_take: It fits the hand like it was waiting for it.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CursedBlade_Res_bury: The stream goes on murmuring where the sword was.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeWhispers_Text: Since the sword came to the colony, the sleepers talk in their sleep, always the same phrase in a language no one speaks. The one who carries it says the blade has asked for a name. It is not a good sign when a blade asks for a name.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeWhispers_Res_name: The blade is pleased. That is the problem.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeWhispers_Res_silence: The chest hums for three nights, then goes still.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeExorcism_Label: Ridding the sword of its voice
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeExorcism_Text: An alchemist of the Heavenly Cauldron who happens to be passing says that a voice in a blade is just a memory, and that every memory can be burned away by the right fire. For the fee of a simple meal she will sit with the blade beside her brazier for a night, and it will either forget or be forgotten.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeExorcism_Res_sit: At dawn the sword is just a sword, and the alchemist looks twenty years older.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BladeExorcism_Res_refuse: The blade will sing again. Pray it does not sing for blood.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DemonBargain_Text: A woman in crimson is waiting at the edge of the camp. She introduces herself as Su Lanyin, the Saint of Blood, and says that her Venerable would like to make an offer to a cultivator of exceptional promise. It involves a night, a bowl and a very small amount of blood.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DemonBargain_Res_accept: The bowl fills. The cultivator's qi rolls like a tide for a night.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DemonBargain_Res_refuse: She smiles. 'The offer remains', she says.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BloodPactDue_Text: The bowl was only the first payment. Su Lanyin returns exactly as she said she would, with six disciples who are not interested in conversation. The Blood Moon Cult never forgets a debt, and has never once explained its interest rate.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BloodPactDue_Res_pay: The cult takes the stones and leaves. The pact is still in the blood.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BloodPactDue_Res_fight: The disciples draw. 'Then in blood', says Su Lanyin.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WoundedEnemyBegs_Text: After a skirmish your people find a Blood Moon disciple crawling in the grass. He is young. He says he never wanted to be there, that the cult took him from a village, that he can cook, and that he will tell you everything. All of it is possibly true.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WoundedEnemyBegs_Res_spare: He weeps. He cooks very well.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WoundedEnemyBegs_Res_execute: A cold quiet falls over the colony. It will pass.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_WoundedEnemyBegs_Res_release: He runs. You will not see him again, or you will.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RivalChallenge_Text: A disciple of the Formless Sword rides in, bows exactly the right amount and challenges your strongest fighter to a duel 'in the spirit of friendship'. Everyone present understands that the spirit of friendship has a very sharp edge.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RivalChallenge_Res_duel: It ends with a tie and a respectful nod. Both leave limping.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_RivalChallenge_Res_decline: The disciple is not offended. He is merely disappointed, which is worse.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_JadeSlipTemptation_Text: A jade slip lies tangled in the roots of an old tree, glowing with a color jade should not glow. A technique of unknown origin is carved into it. The shape of the characters is not one you recognize. Some of your people want to read it. Some of them would like not to.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_JadeSlipTemptation_Res_read: The characters rearrange themselves in the reader's head. It was worth it, mostly.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_JadeSlipTemptation_Res_leave: The tree seems to sigh as the group walks away.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PoorVillageFamine_Text: A delegation from a nearby village stands in the rain, not asking for anything. A cold harvest and no cultivators to bless the fields. The oldest woman says only that she would not have come if there were another door.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PoorVillageFamine_Res_feed: The village sends back a few coins, a basket and a boy to help in the fields.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PoorVillageFamine_Opt_bless: Send a cultivator to bless their fields
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PoorVillageFamine_Res_bless: Their fields thrive. The cultivator learns patience.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PoorVillageFamine_Res_refuse: They bow and leave. You hear the rain a long time.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SacrificeOffer_Label: The offering that should not be accepted
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SacrificeOffer_Text: A shrine appears overnight in the forest, with a bowl and a note: 'a heart for a gift'. The bowl glows. The note is signed by no one. Some of your people think the shrine is a trap. Others think a trap would not bother to be polite.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SacrificeOffer_Res_offer: The bowl accepts. Something shifts in the forest, satisfied.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SacrificeOffer_Res_smash: The shrine breaks like glass. The forest goes very quiet.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CollapsingCave_Text: A tunnel dug by someone long before you collapses with a sound like a sigh. Dust, a few bones, and a rough gate with a seal you recognize from the older stories. Something was walled up here, and now there is a hole to its left.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CollapsingCave_Res_enter: What was walled up was a cache. Probably a cache.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_NightOfTheHungryGhosts_Label: A night for the hungry ghosts
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_NightOfTheHungryGhosts_Text: The seventh moon rises thin and low. Paper lanterns drift through the camp by themselves, bearing names that no one remembers writing. The old customs say to leave a bowl of rice and a stick of incense for each of the hungry dead, and to keep one's own name quiet. This one is going to be a long night.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_NightOfTheHungryGhosts_Res_offer: By dawn the bowls are empty and the lanterns are gone. The camp feels lighter.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_NightOfTheHungryGhosts_Res_ignore: The night is long. Several people sleep with their shoes on.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_AncientCacheMap_Text: A bottle floats down the river and gets caught in the reeds. Inside there is a map, drawn with a trembling hand, to a cache 'for the one who finds this'. A date in an old calendar, a warning to bring someone who can run, and the outline of a mountain that does not look like any mountain nearby.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_AncientCacheMap_Res_go: The expedition leaves at dawn with rope, lanterns and low expectations.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CacheGuardian_Text: At the foot of the mountain there is something that was left to guard. It has been guarding for a long time, and in that time it has forgotten what it was supposed to guard and also what it is. It has not forgotten how to guard.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CacheGuardian_Res_fight: Somewhere in the hills, the guardian is waiting.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CacheVault_Text: With the guardian down, the stone door swings open with a sigh. Inside: dust, three chests, and a skeleton in an old sect robe sitting upright, holding a slip as if it had fallen asleep reading. Perhaps it did.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CacheLost_Text: Weeks later, the mountain slides and the cache goes with it. Maybe it was never there. The map is still on the wall, a bit faded.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionWindWolf_Label: A bounty on the wind wolf
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionWindWolf_Text: A notice nailed to a stake by the road offers a reward to anyone who can bring down the wind wolf of the northern ridge. It has been killing flocks, and the notice is signed by a shepherd who cannot write: she made a drawing of the wolf. It is a very good drawing.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionWolfDone_Text: The shepherd arrives with her flock and a basket of cheese. She says the pasture is quiet again. She also leaves a pouch with a wind wolf's core, which the hunters of her village keep for people who do the job properly.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionWolfFail_Label: The wolf is still out there
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionWolfFail_Text: The notice has been taken down and replaced with a new one: fewer sheep, more sorrow. Nobody mentions your name, which is somehow worse.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionCaravanEscort_Text: A Pavilion caravan will camp one night near your colony and asks for your people to stand watch. Bandits have been seen. The caravan master smiles too widely, which usually means the bandits have been seen a lot closer than he says.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionCaravanEscort_Res_guard: The night is quiet until it isn't.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionEscortReward_Text: In the morning the caravan master counts his carts, finds them all, and pays double what he promised. A man who has been saved from bandits is generous for exactly one day.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionStolenManual_Text: A message from a righteous sect: a gang of rogue thieves has stolen a manual from their library and is hiding in the hills south of your land. They ask you to retrieve it and offer you a copy of the manual's lesser chapters in return.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionStolenManual_Res_go: The thieves are waiting. They always are.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MissionManualReward_Text: You have retrieved the manual, slightly stained with tea and slightly used as a tray. The sect receives it with a grave bow and keeps their word: here are the lesser chapters, in a copy as careful as any scribe could make.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_TravelingHealer_Text: A woman with a satchel of dried herbs says she was a healer in the Heavenly Cauldron Pavilion's infirmary until she grew tired of putting a price on every remedy. She does not want money. She wants a place to stay for the winter and a reason to stop walking.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_TravelingHealer_Res_welcome: She looks around the colony for a long time and finally sets her satchel down.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_TravelingHealer_Opt_food: Give her a meal and let her go
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldMasterRiddle_Text: An old man draws water from your well and says, to no one in particular, 'What is heavy to carry and light to forget?' Then he waits. Several people answer. He shakes his head at each answer with infinite kindness.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldMasterRiddle_Res_humility: He smiles for the first time. 'Almost', he says, and walks away, leaving a feeling like a door that has been propped open.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldMasterRiddle_Res_silence: The old man nods, as if that were the right answer, and goes.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldGraveOpened_Text: A week of rain has washed the topsoil off an old mound, and there is a coffin of lacquered wood, intact. The name on the lid is that of a disciple who died in the Great Rupture. In the coffin: a sword, a pouch of stones, and a short note: 'to whoever, kindly'.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldGraveOpened_Res_take: The gifts are taken. The rain does not stop for three days.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OldGraveOpened_Res_rebury: A small funeral. A very quiet night. Somebody leaves an offering on the mound.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanOfTheCalamity_Text: Searching the ruins of a burned shrine, your people find a girl of seven who has not spoken in days. She clutches a small bronze mirror and does not let go. When someone approaches she looks past them, as if there were somebody standing behind.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanOfTheCalamity_Res_adopt: She sleeps in the corner of the kitchen with the mirror under her cheek.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanOfTheCalamity_Res_lotus: The Pavilion takes her in as an apprentice, with gentleness, a bowl of rice and a contract.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanSpeaks_Text: One morning the girl asks, in a small clear voice, for tea. Then she tells you that the mirror shows the dead as they were. She does not ask what it means. She asks whether she may keep it.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanSpeaks_Res_keep: She smiles for the first time. The mirror glints.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanSpeaks_Res_study: What the mirror shows takes some time to digest.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_OrphanLegacy_Text: A stranger arrives with a letter from a sect that no longer exists. It names the girl as the last heir of a small lineage of mirror-smiths. There is a hidden workshop and a debt that follows the name. The girl listens to all of it, patiently, holding your hand.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudProvocation_Text: A message arrives from a nearby sect, written in a style that is polite until it is not. It claims that your people have 'diluted the dignity of the way' and suggests that things be settled in public. It is signed by a disciple who is clearly not the one in charge.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudProvocation_Res_answer: Your reply is two lines long and uses no adjectives. Their reply is a bruise on the horizon.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudProvocation_Res_apologize: They accept the tea. It is not clear if they accept the apology.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudChallenge_Text: The rival sect appears at dawn in formation, banners high. A herald reads a challenge so long that two of the horses fall asleep. The terms: a public duel between champions, or a fight between everyone. The herald hopes, loudly, for the former.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudChallenge_Res_champion: The champion returns on their own two feet. Mostly.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudChallenge_Res_all: Banners fall, steel rings, and nobody remembers the herald's speech.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_FeudAftermath_Text: The rival sect sends a final message: an invitation to share tea in neutral territory. The tea is not good. The conversation is the best you have had in months. Peace, you realize, is mostly a matter of someone being willing to pour first.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PreStrangeDreams_Text: Three people in the colony tell the same dream at breakfast: a door that opens on a city of towers and a voice that asks, patiently, if they are ready. None of them remembers answering. All of them woke up hungry.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PreStrangeDreams_Res_listen: The pages are, for some reason, in a handwriting not your own.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CauldronCreditors_Text: The Pavilion remembers its debts, including those of an alchemist who fled with the formula for a pill that never worked. Two collectors in silk arrive with a ledger, a polite smile and an extremely long list of fees for 'administration of the debt'.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CauldronCreditors_Res_pay: The ledger closes like a mouth.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_CauldronCreditors_Res_flee: The collectors take off their silk gloves.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_LotusWelcome_Text: A small procession of the Heavenly Cauldron Pavilion arrives, with a censer and a ledger. They bring news that the Pavilion has heard of the exiled healers and has decided that its infirmary has a place for them, whenever they wish it. Mo Qinghua sends tea, and Qian Wanli sends the bill for the tea.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_BeastGuildOffer_Text: A guild of beast hunters sends a representative who wants to meet people capable of tracking a mountain wolf. The guild is not rich, but pays in cores. He shakes your hand too long and, when you ask what's wrong, says only: 'it's the third wolf this month'.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HonestThief_Text: A thin man is caught with a sack of rice from your stores. He does not run. He says he took exactly what his children needed for a week and not a grain more, and offers his services as a servant until the debt is cleared. Nobody has ever seen a thief so precise about his own crime.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HonestThief_Res_hire: He works hard and sleeps by the door, and checks it twice every night.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_HonestThief_Opt_forgive: Let him go with the rice
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MonkInTheRain_Text: A monk sits unmoving at the edge of your land in a downpour. He has been there since dawn. He says he is waiting for the rain to finish, so he can ask it what it wanted. He accepts no shelter. He asks if you would like to wait with him.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_MonkInTheRain_Res_wait: The rain stops at dusk. He says it wanted to be listened to. He leaves with the dry end of the sunset.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectWarAppeal_Text: The old quarrel between {FACTION_name} and {OTHER_name} has finally come to blows. Messengers from both gates reach your colony within the same hour, each with a different version of the same story and the same request: do not leave this to the other side. The war will burn itself out in a couple of weeks, but how it ends may depend on a small thing.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectWarAppeal_Res_aidA: Their messenger bows to the ground. The other gate will not forget.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectWarAppeal_Res_aidB: Their messenger bows to the ground. The other gate will not forget.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectWarAppeal_Res_mediate: The elders agree to sit at the same table. Whether they stay seated is another matter.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTournament_Text: {FACTION_name} and {OTHER_name} are holding a tournament on neutral ground and have sent you a banner with an invitation: send a champion, or at least a witness. The winner takes the season's mountain pass tolls. The loser takes a story to tell about it.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTournament_Res_champion: Win or lose, the champion comes back with a bruise and a better stance.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTournament_Res_watch: The witness returns with a very long story and a very short report.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTribute_Text: Envoys of {FACTION_name} arrive under a banner of good manners. They remind you that the mountain is theirs by old right and that those who graze under it pay a tithe, only a little, only this once. They say it the way you say things that will be said again.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTribute_Res_pay: They count the spirit stones twice, hold one up to the light, and leave without hurry.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTribute_Res_bargain: Half the price and a promise it will not be repeated. Both parties know how much that promise weighs.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_SectTribute_Res_refuse: They bow, correctly, and leave without a word. Correctly is a bad sign.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DisciplesTransfer_Text: A young disciple of {FACTION_name} stands at your gate with a sealed letter from his master: the sect cannot teach him what he needs, and the master hopes your colony can. It is an honorable arrangement, with a price, and the master would like to be remembered for it. The boy would like to be fed.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DisciplesTransfer_Res_accept: He bows to the colony, to the master's letter and to the rice, in that order.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_DisciplesTransfer_Res_decline: The boy takes the letter back and the road with it.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameStep1_Text: The jade that the Master left in your care has been warm for three nights. Tonight it speaks, not in words, but in the weight of a hand on your shoulder: a door, at the edge of your land, that was closed by a man who wanted to be remembered. The jade does not say whether it wants you to open it. It only says that it is time.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameStep2_Text: The founder's seal glows in your hand, and the glow points upward. The old man who closed the tomb left a word on the back of the disc, and the word is a place: a fragment of the broken Celestial Realm, high above the clouds. Those who have a way to rise will find its door. Those who do not will find that the sky, in time, comes down to meet them.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameStep3_Label: The shard points to the field
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameStep3_Text: The shard of Jiuxiao, once carried back to earth, turns slowly in its cradle like a compass looking for north. North is a place the chronicles do not name: the field where the sky was broken. The old sects say nobody has walked it in a thousand years, and that the metal there still remembers how to move.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameStep4_Text: The core of the Rupture was humming when you took it. Now it is silent, and the silence has a shape: a staircase down, deeper than any realm you have walked. At the bottom, the heavens have kept a room for those who would sit in their seat. The jade, finally, stops being warm. It has done what it was made to do.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_EndgameChoice_Text: The seal, the shard, the core and the key lie on one table, and the table is very quiet. Whoever holds them can end the story in one of three ways. One can rise: the highest cultivator among you crosses the last tribulation and ascends, and the colony watches the light go up. One can seal: close the rift above the world for good, so that the storms of qi and the sky of Jiuxiao are forgotten, and the Rimworld goes back to being only the Rimworld. One can rule: sit in the empty Celestial seat and make the old sects bow, at the price of waking what the Rupture put to sleep. Take your time. The keys will not spoil.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetHeirs_Text: Three travellers in the grey of the Thousand Strings Valley arrive at your gate, and they do not look at you. They look at the puppets. They say the valley's workshop belongs to the valley, and that the puppets are its apprentices, and that a thread tied around a living heart is a theft if no one in the valley knows it. The eldest says it flatly, like a fact they are tired of repeating. The youngest has a puppet's hand tattooed on her wrist.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetHeirs_Res_share: They stay three days and teach you the knot that the valley kept for itself.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetHeirs_Res_refuse: The youngest turns at the gate and says, quietly, that the valley has a crypt, and that the crypt remembers.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetHeirs_Res_pay: They count the silver as if it were a funeral fee, and thank you in the same tone.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetCrypt_Text: In the night the ground near your colony settles with a sound like a held breath. At dawn a stone door stands open in the hillside, and the first puppets of the valley, wood stained black with centuries, are lined up in the dark with their hands at their sides. They are not hostile. They are waiting for someone to tell them what to do.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetCrypt_Res_claim: The oldest puppet bows and offers you a roll of silk the thickness of a finger: a blueprint.
LanguageData.CVG_Ev_PuppetCrypt_Res_seal: The door closes like a mouth. For a week, the puppets in your colony stand a little straighter.
